#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Show OpenClaw's own Chrome on the Windows desktop (WSLg :0) long enough for
# its owner to sign in to chat.deepseek.com, then put it back on the hidden
# Xvfb :9. The switch is a runtime drop-in: it is removed on exit, and a distro
# restart drops it anyway, so the persistent :9 setup is never edited.
set -u
TIMEOUT_S="${SIGNIN_TIMEOUT:-900}"
UNIT=openclaw-gateway.service
DROP="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/$(id -u)}/systemd/user/$UNIT.d"
B="openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw"
PATH_JS='() => location.pathname'

restore() {
  rm -f "$DROP/20-deepseek-sign-in.conf"
  systemctl --user daemon-reload
  systemctl --user restart "$UNIT"
  echo "[sign-in] browser back on the hidden display"
}

wait_gateway() {
  for _ in $(seq 1 90); do $B status >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0; sleep 1; done
  return 1
}

pathname() {
  $B --timeout 30000 evaluate --json --timeout-ms 20000 --fn "$PATH_JS" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -o '"result": *"[^"]*"' | sed 's/.*"\([^"]*\)"$/\1/'
}

mkdir -p "$DROP"
printf '[Service]\nEnvironment=DISPLAY=:0\n' > "$DROP/20-deepseek-sign-in.conf"
trap restore EXIT
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user restart "$UNIT"
wait_gateway || { echo "[sign-in] FAIL: gateway did not come back"; exit 2; }

OK=0; for _ in $(seq 1 60); do $B open https://chat.deepseek.com/sign_in >/dev/null 2>&1 && { OK=1; break; }; sleep 1; done
[ "$OK" = 1 ] || { echo "[sign-in] FAIL: could not open DeepSeek"; exit 3; }
echo "[sign-in] DeepSeek sign-in window is open on the desktop. Waiting up to ${TIMEOUT_S}s for sign-in..."

T0=$(date +%s)
while :; do
  P="$(pathname)"
  case "$P" in
    ""|/sign_in*|/sign_up*) ;;
    *) echo "[sign-in] signed in (page: $P)"; break ;;
  esac
  if [ $(( $(date +%s) - T0 )) -ge "$TIMEOUT_S" ]; then echo "[sign-in] TIMEOUT: still on sign-in page"; exit 4; fi
  sleep 3
done
sleep 3  # let the session cookie settle before Chrome is restarted
exit 0
EOF
cat > $D/deepseek-live-check.ts <<'EOF'
// One live DeepSeek round trip through the real gateway; prints the reply or the reason.
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { resolveOptions } from '../src/index.ts'
import { buildSpec, parseReply } from '../src/transport.ts'

const options = resolveOptions({ site: 'deepseek' })
const spec = buildSpec(options, 'Reply with exactly: PONG', AbortSignal.timeout(300_000))
const t0 = Date.now()
const child = spawn(spec.argv[0]!, spec.argv.slice(1), { stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'inherit'] })
let out = ''
child.stdout.on('data', (d: Buffer) => { out += d.toString() })
child.stdin.end((spec.stdio as { stdin: { data: string } }).stdin.data)
child.on('close', () => {
  const seconds = ((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1)
  try {
    console.log(`[live-check] DeepSeek replied in ${seconds}s: ${JSON.stringify(parseReply(out))}`)
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(`[live-check] FAIL after ${seconds}s: ${(error as Error).message}`)
    process.exitCode = 1
  }
})
EOF

reply block". Small prompts stay inline; a larger one is appended into the
page in 100 KB chunks, one evaluate each, and the turn reads it back only if
it arrived whole (a short one fails step 24 instead of sending a fragment).

on DeepSeek (57.6s) and ChatGPT (36.8s).

Keep idle Anthropic streams alive and stop thinking-only recoveries

NVIDIA NIM MiniMax buffers native tool-call markup until the call closes,
and midstream recovery buffers its whole continuation, so a large Write
left Claude Code clients with minutes of silence; they dropped the stream
and burned their retries. Emit Messages API ping frames every 10 s while
the provider body is idle.

A cut-off turn whose recovery produced only thinking was reported as a
successful end_turn, which silently ended headless agent loops. Treat it
as a failed recovery so the client retries.

Rate-limit cooldown goes from 120 s to 600 s: Gemini quota 429s outlast
the old window, so each request wasted ~33 s retrying a dead model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

import re,sys
def hunks(path):

    return s,pat
# assessment.js

res=[]
def f(m):
    res.append((m.group(1),m.group(2)));i=len(res)
    h,t=m.group(1),m.group(2)

    if i==2:
        # keep HEAD SAM text, then theirs tariff text minus the shared first line
        t2=t.replace("// admin-tunable (see lib/settings.js).\n","",1)
        return h.replace("//\n// SAM","//\n// SAM",1)+"//\n"+t2 if False else h+"//\n"+t2
    if i==3:
        return "export async function assessProperty({ lat, lng, areaSqFt, propertyType, hasNetMeteringAgreement = false }) {\n  const [costPerWattUsd, phpPerUsd] = await Promise.all([\n"
    if i==4:
        return ("    // Preserved: null for a system that never pays back (or has no evidenced tariff);\n"
 "    // paybackYearsLabel is always MODEL_BASELINE so a null still reads as the baseline's answer.\n"
 "    paybackYears: revenue != null ? finiteOrNull(paybackYears({ installCostUsd: cost, annualRevenueUsd: revenue })) : null,\n"
 "    paybackYearsLabel: PAYBACK_BASELINE_LABEL,\n"
 "    roiPercent: revenue != null ? roiPercent({ installCostUsd: cost, annualRevenueUsd: revenue }) : null,\n")
s=pat.sub(f,s)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(s)
# route
p='app/api/properties/[id]/assess/route.js'
s,pat=hunks(p)
def g(m):
    return ("    // sam: six SAM scenario paths (or { available: false, reason }), supplementary to the USD baseline.\n"
"    // paybackYearsLabel rides in raw (no column). tariff: which tariff priced annualRevenueUsd\n"

"      tariff: { mode: result.tariffMode, reason: result.tariffReason, tariffVersionId: result.tariffVersionId },\n")
s=pat.sub(g,s)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='').write(s)
EOF

# Neighborhood Tech: end-to-end test plan (WP9)

Scope: Oakland/East Bay pilot, EN/ES, local only, no deploy. Automated suite: `npm test` (node:test, no network, no real credentials). Everything marked MANUAL needs a human, a device or a live third-party account and is a launch-gate item, not an automated check.

## Automated layers

| Layer | Where | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| Unit and module API | `test/<module>/*.test.js` | Each module's rules: money, ledger, booking states, review clock, PII guard, signatures |
| Site integration | `test/integration/site.test.js` | Every module loads into one app, every page serves, a11y landmarks, EN/ES key parity |
| Launch gate | `test/integration/launch-gate.test.js` | Safety defaults hold (test-mode payments, Meta dry run and $100 cap, ntfy off when unset), admin routes reject anonymous callers, and these docs plus `docs/launch-gates.json` stay consistent with the code |

## Journeys (each runs in the suite unless marked MANUAL)

1. Guest lead: guest submits intent form, lead stored, kpi `lead_created`.
2. Account and household: register, login, create household, invite member.
3. Quote to paid: tech creates quote, customer approves, order, payment, receipt EN/ES, ledger balances (trial balance zero).
4. Booking: slots appear only for techs on duty, hold, confirm, double booking refused (409), cancel cutoff 1 h, reschedule.
5. Plan review: request, tech start (server clock), stop within 20 min, or overdue escalation, admin logs refund decision (Q16).
6. AI intake: rate limit, per-customer cost cap, PII redaction, tier 2 needs tech approval, handoff.
7. Channels: inbound webhook signature verified, case created, STOP/ALTO opt-out honoured.
8. Remote support: one-time code, consent checkbox, expiry, end session. Real remote tool = MANUAL (G4).
9. Backups: subscribe, chunked upload, encrypt, restore byte-identical, quota, grace expiry with injected clock.
10. Meta: dry run default, everything PAUSED, $100 cap, webhook signature, CAPI hashing only.
11. Growth: referral code, redemption, fraud rules, credits ledger.

## Cross-cutting checks (all automated)

- Accessibility structure: lang, skip link, main landmark, viewport, shared CSS, language toggle on every page.
- i18n: identical non-empty EN and ES keys; every `data-i18n` key exists in its dictionary; no markup in plain-text keys.
- Security: anonymous requests to admin routes return 401; Stripe refuses `sk_live_` and unknown keys; webhooks reject bad signatures; backups encrypted at rest.
- Money: integer cents only; refunds cannot exceed paid.

## MANUAL checks (owner: a human, evidence in the launch-gate record)

- Browser pass EN and ES at 320 px, 200% zoom, keyboard only, with a screen reader on the home, booking and checkout pages.
- Stripe test-mode checkout with a real `sk_test_` key and the Stripe CLI webhook (G3).
- Real ntfy topic receives a booking alert and an escalation alert.
- iPhone remote session limited to screen viewing and guided steps (G4).
- Real SMS/WhatsApp round trip (G5).
- Restore drill on the real NAS target (G6).
- Meta test event visible in Events Manager with `test_event_code`; no ad leaves PAUSED without human approval (G5, G7).

## Entry and exit

Entry: `npm test` is green (exit code 0, zero failures) on the commit under test.
Exit for a beta stage: every automated layer green, all MANUAL checks for that stage signed off, and the launch gates for that stage satisfied (see `docs/launch-gates.md`).
EOF
cat > docs/runbooks.md <<'EOF'
# Neighborhood Tech runbooks

Single Node 22.5+ process, node:sqlite, no external services required. Start: `npm start` (port 4700). Health: `GET /api/health` returns `{ ok, modules, now }`.

## Configuration (environment)

| Variable | Purpose | Safe default when unset |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | HTTP port | 4700 |
| `DB_FILE` | SQLite file | `data/nt.db` when run via `npm start` |
| `NT_NTFY_TOPIC` | ntfy topic for tech alerts | alerts disabled |
| `NT_NTFY_SERVER` | ntfy server | `https://ntfy.sh` |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Stripe key, test keys only (`sk_test_`) | checkout refused (503), never mock |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Stripe webhook signing secret | webhooks rejected |
| `NT_PAYMENTS_MOCK` | `1` enables mock provider (tests only) | off |
| `NT_BACKUP_ROOT` | Backup storage directory | `data/backups` |
| `NT_BACKUP_MASTER_KEY` | Master key wrapping per-customer backup keys | dev key generated into settings |
| `NT_META_DRY_RUN` | Meta dry run | on (`1`) |
| `NT_META_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Meta token | not configured |
| `NT_META_APP_SECRET` | Meta webhook signing secret | generated into settings |
| `NT_META_VERIFY_TOKEN` | Meta webhook verify token | generated into settings |
| `NT_META_PIXEL_ID` | CAPI pixel | not configured |

Never commit these. Production values stay outside the repo.

## RB-1 Start, stop, health
1. `npm start`; expect the log line `Neighborhood Tech on http://localhost:4700`.
2. `GET /api/health`: `ok` true and every module in the list.
3. Stop with Ctrl+C; SQLite WAL is safe to stop at any time.

## RB-2 Tech alert silent (ntfy)
Cause is almost always `NT_NTFY_TOPIC` unset: adapter reports `ntfy_not_configured` and drops alerts. Set the topic and restart. Escalations from the plan-review clock use priority 5.

## RB-3 Plan review overdue (20-minute clock, Q16)
1. A review running past 20 minutes escalates on the next read or `POST /api/scheduling/admin/reviews/sweep`, and sends a priority-5 alert.
2. Admin lists `GET /api/scheduling/admin/reviews?status=escalated`.
3. Admin logs the decision: `POST /api/scheduling/admin/reviews/:id/decision` with `decision` (`refund` or `no_refund`), `reason`, and `amount_cents` for refunds. One decision per review; it is in the audit log.
4. A logged `refund` does not move money. Issue it with `POST /api/orders/:id/refund` using the same amount.

## RB-4 Payments not working
- 503 "not configured": set a `sk_test_` key. Live keys are refused by design.
- Webhook 400: check `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and clock skew under 5 minutes.
- Ledger check: trial balance must be zero (`trialBalance` in `src/lib/ledger.js`; covered by `test/payments/money-ledger.test.js`).

## RB-5 Double booking report
Bookings are protected inside `tx()` and by slot status. Check `scheduling_bookings` for two `held`/`confirmed` rows on one `slot_id`; if present, cancel the later one through the admin booking endpoint and open a bug.

## RB-6 Backups
- Grace expiry job: `POST /api/backups/admin/run-expiry`.
- Losing `NT_BACKUP_MASTER_KEY` makes encrypted backups unrecoverable. Keep an offline copy before taking any real customer file.

## RB-7 Meta spend
Dry run is on by default and every ad is created PAUSED. The $100 lifetime cap (10,000 cents) is enforced in code. Do not set `NT_META_DRY_RUN=0` without gate G7 approval.

## RB-8 Incident and data handling
1. Stop the process if customer data exposure is suspected.
2. Preserve `data/nt.db` and the audit log (`audit_log` table) untouched; copy before any change.
3. Record time, scope and actions in the shared agent log; notify the owner.
EOF
cat > docs/rollback.md <<'EOF'
# Neighborhood Tech rollback

State lives in three places: git (code), `data/nt.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`), and `NT_BACKUP_ROOT` (encrypted customer files). Schema is additive only (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), so older code runs against a newer database; new tables are simply ignored.

## Before every release
1. Stop the process (so WAL is checkpointed) or use the SQLite online backup.
2. Copy `data/nt.db`, `data/nt.db-wal`, `data/nt.db-shm` to `data/bak-<date>-<reason>/` (the repo already uses this pattern, e.g. `data/bak-2026-10-31-stale-scheduling`).
3. Copy `NT_BACKUP_ROOT` if backups are in use.
4. Note the current commit: `git rev-parse HEAD`.

## Code rollback
1. `git revert <bad-sha>` (new commit) or deploy the recorded previous commit. Never rewrite published history.
2. `npm test`; exit code must be 0.
3. Restart and check `GET /api/health`.

## Data rollback
1. Stop the process.
2. Move the live `data/nt.db*` aside to `data/bak-<date>-failed/`.
3. Restore the pre-release copy.
4. Start and verify health, then spot check one booking, one order and the audit log.
5. Data written between backup and rollback is lost: export it from the aside copy first if it matters.

## Feature kill switches (no redeploy)
| Risk | Switch |
|---|---|
| Payments | Unset `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`: checkout refuses with 503 |
| Meta spend | Keep `NT_META_DRY_RUN` on; all ads stay PAUSED |
| Alerts | Unset `NT_NTFY_TOPIC` |
| Booking | Techs set duty state `off`; no slots are offered |

## What not to roll back
The audit log and ledger are append-only records. Correct mistakes with a new entry (refund, reversal, new decision note), never by deleting rows.
EOF
